intent: The doctors-per-person misdirect: Germany has the hospitals and America the money, but a Caribbean island of 11 million trains more doctors per head than anyone — shown as three bars, undercut by a counter that falls as its doctors leave, and finished with the pin and the export nobody expects.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which nation has the MOST doctors per person?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which nation has the most doctors per person?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Cuba. More than 9 doctors for every 1,000 people, the highest ratio on Earth.

lines.direction: pull right out over the Atlantic; the three bars grow on 'Germany' — Cuba, Germany, United States — with the stethoscope sticker; the thinking US flag-ball drops in on 'States' and the answer pulses on 'hospitals'
lines.text: Germany has fewer than 5. The United States, for all its hospitals, has under 4.

lines.direction: push back onto the island; the counter starts at 106,131 on 'peak' and falls to 75,364 by 'left'; the island sticker and the 11-million tag on 'million'; the door sticker replaces it on 'left' with a pulse
lines.text: At its peak the island had over 100,000 doctors for 11 million people. Since then, tens of thousands have left.

lines.direction: pull out over the Caribbean and Latin America; the 37,000 card on 'abroad'; the plane sticker and the 50+ countries tag on 'countries'; the happy Cuban flag-ball pulse on 'income'
lines.text: Cuba also sends doctors abroad: around 37,000 work in other countries, its main source of foreign income.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
